record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: Can one give an ergodic-theoretic proof of the equidistribution of special points on SL_2(Z)\H^2?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 59 (L. Silberman). Give an ergodic-theoretic proof of the equidistribu-tion of special points on SL2(Z)\H2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}^2 = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \mathrm{Im}(z) > 0\}$ denote the upper half-plane, on which $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ acts by Möbius transformations, and let $Y = \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) ackslash \mathbb{H}^2$ denote the modular curve, equipped with the hyperbolic probability measure $d\mu_{\mathrm{hyp}} =  rac{3}{\pi}  rac{dx\, dy}{y^2}$ on a fundamental domain.

A point $z \in \mathbb{H}^2$ is called a special point (or CM point) if $z$ is a quadratic irrational; equivalently, $z$ is a fixed point of some element of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ of trace zero, and corresponds to an elliptic curve with complex multiplication by an order in an imaginary quadratic field. To each negative fundamental discriminant $D < 0$ one associates the finite set $\Lambda_D \subset Y$ of special points of discriminant $D$, whose cardinality is the class number $h(D)$.

It is known (theorem of Duke, building on partial results of Linnik) that the uniform probability measures $\mu_D =  rac{1}{|\Lambda_D|} \sum_{z \in \Lambda_D} \delta_z$ converge weak-$*$ to $\mu_{\mathrm{hyp}}$ as $D 	o -\infty$ through fundamental discriminants. Duke's proof proceeds via subconvex bounds for $L$-functions and modular forms.

Problem. Give a proof of the equidistribution statement
$$\mu_D \xrightarrow{\;w^*\;} \mu_{\mathrm{hyp}} \qquad 	ext{as } D 	o -\infty,$$
using only ergodic-theoretic methods (for instance, measure rigidity for diagonal or torus actions on homogeneous spaces, joinings, or unipotent dynamics), without appealing to subconvexity of $L$-functions.
artifact.status_search_result: An ergodic-theoretic approach to equidistribution of CM/special points was developed by Linnik (under a splitting hypothesis) and extended by Einsiedler, Lindenstrauss, Michel, and Venkatesh, who used measure rigidity for torus actions on homogeneous spaces to give ergodic-theoretic proofs of equidistribution of toral/CM packets (under mild auxiliary splitting conditions), and the unconditional result is by Duke. Thus an ergodic-theoretic proof of equidistribution of special points on the modular surface is generally regarded as available, although the fully unconditional Duke-strength theorem still required input beyond pure ergodic theory in some regimes.

status_evidence.title: Equidistribution, L-functions and Ergodic theory: on some problems of Linnik
status_evidence.snippet: Einsiedler, Lindenstrauss, Michel and Venkatesh introduce a variant of Linnik's ergodic method, in the framework of homogeneous dynamics, applied to equidistribution of CM points.
status_evidence.claim: An ergodic-theoretic proof of equidistribution of special (CM) points on SL_2(Z)\H exists via measure rigidity / Linnik's ergodic method, under splitting hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: Joint equidistribution of CM points
status_evidence.snippet: Einsiedler, Lindenstrauss, Michel and Venkatesh proved equidistribution results for toral packets/CM points using homogeneous dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Ergodic methods (homogeneous dynamics, measure rigidity) yield equidistribution of CM points on arithmetic quotients including the modular surface.

status_evidence.title: Linnik's ergodic method and the distribution of integer points on spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Ellenberg–Michel–Venkatesh: Linnik's ergodic method and equidistribution.
status_evidence.claim: Linnik's original ergodic method gives equidistribution of special points under a splitting condition.
